documents: Decuypère, Tremblay & Dufour (2022), Impact of Ocean Heat Transport on Arctic Sea Ice Variability in the GFDL CM2-O Model Suite, JGR Oceans 127, e2021JC017762 (published PDF, 22 pp.)

entry.evidence: relatively fewer studies focus on the impact of resolution on OHT and SIE variability in the Arctic Ocean

sequences.source_document: Decuypère et al. 2022, JGR Oceans, published PDF

steps.action: Take from other model studies the expectation that finer ocean resolution increases poleward OHT and lowers Arctic SIE.
steps.quote: Several studies showed that an increase in resolution leads to an increase in midlatitude meridional ocean heat transport (OHT)

steps.action: Pose the question of how refining ocean horizontal resolution in CM2-O affects Arctic OHT, SIE and their relationship.
steps.quote: We investigate the impact of refining the horizontal grid spacing of the ocean component on OHT in the Arctic, SIE and their relationship.

steps.action: Use the three CM2-O configurations (1°, 1/4°, 1/10°), each with a 200-year preindustrial control and an 80-year 1%/yr CO2 run branched at year 121, one member each.
steps.quote: We analyze a preindustrial control run and a climate change run for each configuration

steps.action: Compute OHT from the online diagnostic, integrated across four gates defined on the Low-resolution grid, together with SIE from the model output.
steps.quote: The OHT at each gate is calculated by integrating the monthly or yearly averaged OHT across the gate and the full water column.

steps.action: Check that gate positioning changes OHT magnitude only slightly and uniformly across configurations and leaves variability unchanged (results not shown).
steps.quote: the positioning has a negligible impact on the variability (not shown)

steps.action: Compare simulated ice thickness, SIE, gate OHT and 26.5°N OHT with submarine, satellite, presatellite and mooring estimates, aligned by equivalent CO2 concentration.
steps.quote: Over the observational period, the Medium resolution is the closest to the observational estimates of total OHT and SIE

steps.action: Attribute the very low Barents Sea Opening OHT in Low to atmospheric circulation rather than resolution, citing other 1° models with higher OHT.
steps.quote: This is presumably due to discrepancies in the large-scale atmospheric circulation

steps.action: Rank the three configurations to state that higher OHT goes with lower SIE across the suite.
steps.quote: Hence, in the CM2-O model suite, the greater the OHT, the lower the SIE

steps.action: Describe the SIE decline and OHT increase under CO2 forcing in each configuration, including trends and decadal signals.
steps.quote: all configurations show a linear decline in SIE with a clear decadal to multidecadal

steps.action: Compare trends against preindustrial states to show that Medium's lower SIE comes from its mean state, and that High responds more strongly than Low.
steps.quote: the lower SIE at the end of the CC run in the Medium resolution is mostly due to the preindustrial mean state

steps.action: Compute 20-year moving-window correlations between detrended total OHT and May and September SIE, with 95% significance, for each configuration.
steps.quote: the total OHT is significantly correlated with May SIE in the Low resolution from year 23 until year 38

steps.action: Take from earlier work the expectation that weak air-sea coupling at low resolution should strengthen the ice-edge and OHT correlation.
steps.quote: This weak atmosphere-ocean coupling should in principle lead to stronger correlation between ice edge location and OHT variability

steps.action: Explain the missing coupling in Low by its near-zero Barents Sea Opening OHT rather than abandon the OHT-SIE link.
steps.quote: The absence of SIE-OHT coupling in the Low resolution is instead attributed to the very small OHT

steps.action: Check the interannual links in the CTRL simulation and find them only intermittently present (results not shown).
steps.quote: are not always present in the CTRL simulation (not shown)

steps.action: Narrow the claim to a regional driver: OHT variability drives sea ice variability mainly when ice extends into the Barents Sea.
steps.quote: This suggests that OHT variability is a major driver of sea ice variability at regional scale

steps.action: Correlate decadal OHT at the Fram Strait, Barents Sea Opening and Bering Strait with sector SIE in each configuration.
steps.quote: with a significant-correlation coefficients of −0.92 between the September SIE and the Fram Strait and Barents Sea Opening OHT

steps.action: Map correlations between gate OHT and detrended May SIC, identifying tripole and NAO-linked dipole patterns.
steps.quote: We now turn to spatial correlations between OHT and Sea Ice Concentration (SIC) anomalies

steps.action: Vary the month used for SIC and report that correlation intensity changes but the patterns stay similar.
steps.quote: the intensity of the correlation may vary depending on the month used for SIC, but the correlation patterns are similar

steps.action: Ask why OHT falls from Medium to High resolution, a result that conflicts with other model studies.
steps.quote: This nonmonotonic behavior with spatial resolution is in contrast with other studies, which show a systematic increase in OHT with a finer resolution

steps.action: Propose Atlantic Water partitioning among the Barents Sea Opening, Fram Strait and Irminger Current as the main candidate, alongside AMOC, NAO state and atmospheric resolution.
steps.quote: with the main candidate being the different partitioning of Atlantic Waters between the Barents Sea Opening, Fram Strait and Irminger Current

steps.action: Recompute OHT along 60°N and 65°N transects as in earlier studies and report the same conclusion (results not shown).
steps.quote: This conclusion is robust with respect to the exact location where OHT is calculated

steps.action: Set aside AMOC strength as the cause, because Medium has higher OHT despite a weaker AMOC (not shown).
steps.quote: This suggests that the higher OHT in the Medium resolution is linked with the surface ocean circulation (gyre transport) rather than the meridional circulation

steps.action: Map maximum temperature, surface salinity, surface velocity and winter mixed-layer depth in the first decade to compare current pathways (Figure 8).
steps.quote: All three model versions agree broadly in the structure of the currents in northern North Atlantic

steps.action: Take from earlier work the expectation that a more positive NAO in Low and High should push Atlantic Water deeper through the Fram Strait and Barents Sea Opening.
steps.quote: should promote deeper penetration of Atlantic Waters in the Fram Strait and Barents Sea Opening in the Low and High resolutions

steps.action: Reject NAO as the leading factor, because High shows more Irminger recirculation than Medium, contrary to the NAO expectation.
steps.quote: indicating the NAO variability is not the leading factor in determining the current pathways in the Arctic

steps.action: Compare Davis Strait OHT and OVT with observations and show Davis Strait OVT is anticorrelated with Fram Strait plus Barents Sea Opening transport, supporting partitioning.
steps.quote: correlation coefficients of −0.82, −0.96, and −0.82 in the Low, Medium, and High [...]

steps.action: Relate partitioning to deep convection centers: mixed-layer depth maps and OVT-MLD correlation maps show convection shifting from the GIN Seas to the Labrador Sea.
steps.quote: From Low to High resolutions, we see a south-westward transfer of deep convection regions from the Greenland-Icelandic-Norwegian (GIN) Seas toward the Labrador Sea

steps.action: Retain the claims: resolution does not systematically raise Arctic OHT in CM2-O, higher OHT means lower SIE, and the Irminger branch is favored at high resolution.
steps.quote: In the CM2-O model, the refining of spatial resolution does not induce a systematic increase in OHT

end.claim: In the GFDL CM2-O suite, Arctic OHT rises from 1° to 1/4° but falls at 1/10°; this is best explained by Atlantic Water rerouting toward the Irminger Current and Davis Strait and a westward shift of deep convection. Across configurations, higher OHT goes with lower SIE.

decisive_move.sentence: Comparing OHT and SIE across the three resolution configurations and against observations (Table 1, Figure 3) showed that Medium carries about 50% more heat into the Arctic than High, the nonmonotonic result on which the paper rests.

gates.evidence: The simulations were chosen to answer a question about resolution, not directed by a stated hypothesis; partitioning was proposed only after the nonmonotonic result (p. 15). The NAO rival was tested against a cited expectation and rejected (pp. 15-16), but the partitioning explanation rests on correlations and was never exposed to a test it could fail. Nothing was fixed in advance.

imports.item: moving-window correlation of detrended series with 95% significance testing

novelty_claims.quote: In contrast with previous studies, however, the ocean heat transport does not systematically increase when refining the ocean horizontal resolution.
Ocean heat transport into the Arctic does not systematically increase with horizontal resolution in the GFDL CM2-O model suite

limits: Only one ensemble member per configuration, so internal variability cannot be separated from resolution effects. Several checks are reported as 'not shown': gate positioning, the CTRL links, the 60°N and 65°N transects, the AMOC strength and the NAO spin-up state. The paper does not say who ran the simulations; that they were produced by GFDL rather than in this study is inference. Resolution is confounded with the eddy parameterization, which is used only in Low. The authors themselves say other eddy-rich GCMs are needed to test whether the drop from Medium to High is robust (p. 19). Sub-claims and their statuses: higher OHT with lower SIE across the suite, and decadal OHT driving SIE, are regularity_in_range (within the suite, mainly regional, early in the runs); Medium agreeing best with observations is capability_characterized for the model; NAO being excluded as the leading factor rests on one qualitative comparison. Composition is none_fits: a controlled numerical comparison across configurations, followed by post hoc rival explanations, matches no listed walk. No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded.
